See [Version-matched documentation](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#version-matched-documentation) for the managed block and setup details. 00037| 00038| ## Using the codemod 00039| 00040| To update to Next.js version 16, you can use the `upgrade` [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160): 00041| 00042| ```bash package="pnpm" 00043| pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 00044| ``` 00045| 00046| ```bash package="npm" 00047| npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 00048| ``` 00049| 00050| ```bash package="yarn" 00051| yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 00052| ``` 00053| 00054| ```bash package="bun" 00055| bunx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 00056| ``` 00057| 00058| The [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to: 00059| 00060| - Update `next.config.js` to use the new `turbopack` configuration 00061| - Migrate from `next lint` to the ESLint CLI 00062| - Migrate from deprecated `middleware` convention to `proxy` 00063| - Remove `unstable_` prefix from stabilized APIs 00064| - Remove `experimental_ppr` Route Segment Config from pages and layouts 00065| 00066| The `upgrade` codemod does not run every migration codemod. If your app still uses synchronous `params`, `searchParams`, `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `draftMode()` access from the Next.js 15 compatibility period, also run the async Request APIs codemod: 00067| 00068| ```bash filename="Terminal" 00069| npx @next/codemod@canary next-async-request-api . 00070| ``` 00071| 00072| ## Install packages manually 00073| 00074| If you prefer to do it manually, install the latest Next.js and React versions: 00075| 00076| ```bash package="pnpm" 00077| pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 00078| ``` 00079| 00080| ```bash package="npm" 00081| npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 00082| ``` 00083| 00084| ```bash package="yarn" 00085| yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 00086| ``` 00087| 00088| ```bash package="bun" 00089| bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 00090| ``` 00091| 00092| If you are using TypeScript, ensure you also upgrade `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` to their latest versions. 00093| 00094| ## Node.js runtime and browser support 00095| 00096| | Requirement | Change / Details | 00097| | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | 00098| | Node.js 20.9+ | Minimum version now `20.9.0` (LTS); Node.js 18 no longer supported | 00099| | TypeScript 5+ | Minimum version now `5.1.0` | 00100| | Browsers | Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+ | 00101| 00102| ## Turbopack by default 00103| 00104| Starting with **Next.js 16**, Turbopack is stable and used by default with `next dev` and `next build` 00105| 00106| Previously you had to enable Turbopack using `--turbopack`, or `--turbo`. 00107| 00108| ```json filename="package.json" 00109| { 00110| "scripts": { 00111| "dev": "next dev --turbopack", 00112| "build": "next build --turbopack", 00113| "start": "next start" 00114| } 00115| } 00116| ``` 00117| 00118| This is no longer necessary. You can update your `package.json` scripts: 00119| 00120| ```json filename="package.json" 00121| { 00122| "scripts": { 00123| "dev": "next dev", 00124| "build": "next build", 00125| "start": "next start" 00126| } 00127| } 00128| ``` 00129| 00130| If your project has a [custom `webpack`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/webpack) configuration and you run `next build` (which now uses Turbopack by default), the build will **fail** to prevent misconfiguration issues. 00131| 00132| You have a few different ways to address this: 00133| 00134| - **Use Turbopack anyway:** Run with `next build --turbopack` to build using Turbopack and ignore your `webpack` config. 00135| - **Switch to Turbopack fully:** Migrate your `webpack` config to Turbopack-compatible options. 00136| - **Keep using Webpack:** Use the `--webpack` flag to opt out of Turbopack and build with Webpack. 00137| 00138| > **Good to know**: If you see failing builds because a `webpack` configuration was found, but you don't define one yourself, it is likely that a plugin is adding a `webpack` option 00139| 00140| ### Opting out of Turbopack 00141| 00142| If you need to continue using Webpack, you can opt out with the `--webpack` flag. For example, to use Turbopack in development but Webpack for production builds: 00143| 00144| ```json filename="package.json" 00145| { 00146| "scripts": { 00147| "dev": "next dev", 00148| "build": "next build --webpack", 00149| "start": "next start" 00150| } 00151| } 00152| ``` 00153| 00154| We recommend using Turbopack for development and production. Submit a comment to this [thread](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77721), if you are unable to switch to Turbopack. 00155| 00156| ### Turbopack configuration location 00157| 00158| The `experimental.turbopack` configuration is out of experimental. 00159| 00160| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 00161| import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 00162| 00163| // Next.js 15 - experimental.turbopack 00164| const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 00165| experimental: { 00166| turbopack: { 00167| // options 00168| }, 00169| }, 00170| } 00171| 00172| export default nextConfig 00173| ``` 00174| 00175| You can use it as a top-level `turbopack` option: 00176| 00177| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 00178| import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 00179| 00180| // Next.js 16 - turbopack at the top level of nextConfig 00181| const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 00182| turbopack: { 00183| // options 00184| }, 00185| } 00186| 00187| export default nextConfig 00188| ``` 00189| 00190| Make sure to review the `Turbopack` configuration [options](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack). **Next.js 16** introduces various improvements and new options, for example: 00191| 00192| - [Advanced Webpack loader conditions](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#advanced-webpack-loader-conditions) 00193| - [debugIds](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#debug-ids) 00194| 00195| ### Resolve alias fallback 00196| 00197| In some projects, client-side code may import files containing Node.js native modules. This will cause `Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs'` type of errors. 00198| 00199| When this happens, you should refactor your code so that your client-side bundles do not reference these Node.js native modules. 00200| 00201| However, in some cases, this might not be possible. In Webpack the `resolve.fallback` option was typically used to **silence** the error. Turbopack offers a similar option, using `turbopack.resolveAlias`. In this case, tell Turbopack to load an empty module when `fs` is requested for the browser. 00202| 00203| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 00204| import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 00205| 00206| const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 00207| turbopack: { 00208| resolveAlias: { 00209| fs: { 00210| browser: './empty.ts', // We recommend to fix code imports before using this method 00211| }, 00212| }, 00213| }, 00214| } 00215| 00216| export default nextConfig 00217| ``` 00218| 00219| It is preferable to refactor your modules so that client code doesn't ever import from modules using Node.js native modules. 00220| 00221| ### Sass node_modules imports 00222| 00223| Turbopack fully supports importing Sass files from `node_modules`. Note that while Webpack allowed the legacy tilde (`~`) prefix, Turbopack does not support this syntax. 00224| 00225| In Webpack: 00226| 00227| ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 00228| @import '~bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 00229| ``` 00230| 00231| In Turbopack: 00232| 00233| ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 00234| @import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 00235| ``` 00236| 00237| If changing the imports is not possible, you can use `turbopack.resolveAlias`. For example: 00238| 00239| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 00240| import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 00241| 00242| const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 00243| turbopack: { 00244| resolveAlias: { 00245| '~*': '*', 00246| }, 00247| }, 00248| } 00249| 00250| export default nextConfig 00251| ``` 00252| 00253| ### Turbopack File System Caching 00254| 00255| Turbopack stores compiler artifacts on disk between runs, for significantly faster compile times across restarts. Filesystem caching is enabled by default for both `next dev` and `next build`, through `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev` and `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild`. See [Turbopack FileSystem Caching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopackFileSystemCache) to configure or disable either one. 00256| 00257| 00258| 00259| ## Async Request APIs (Breaking change) 00260| 00261| Version 15 introduced [Async Request APIs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-15#async-request-apis-breaking-change) as a breaking change, with **temporary** synchronous compatibility. 00262| 00263| Starting with **Next.js 16**, synchronous access is fully removed. These APIs can only be accessed asynchronously. 00264| 00265| - [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) 00266| - [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) 00267| - [`draftMode`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/draft-mode) 00268| - `params` in [`layout.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [`route.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default), [`opengraph-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#opengraph-image), [`twitter-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#twitter-image), [`icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#icon), and [`apple-icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#apple-icon). 00269| - `searchParams` in [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) 00270| 00271| Use the [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#migrate-to-async-dynamic-apis) to migrate to async Request-time APIs. 00272| 00273| ### Migrating types for async Request-time APIs 00274| 00275| To help migrate to async `params` and `searchParams`, you can run [`npx next typegen`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next#next-typegen-options) to automatically generate these globally available types helpers: 00276| 00277| - [`PageProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) 00278| - [`LayoutProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper) 00279| - [`RouteContext`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#route-context-helper) 00280| 00281| > **Good to know**: `typegen` was introduced in Next.js 15.5 00282| 00283| This simplifies type-safe migration to the new async API pattern, and enables you to update your components with full type safety, for example: 00284| 00285| ```tsx filename="/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" 00286| export default async function Page(props: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) { 00287| const { slug } = await props.params 00288| const query = await props.searchParams 00289| return

Blog Post: {slug}

00290| } 00291| ``` 00292| 00293| This approach gives you fully type-safe access to `props.params`, including the `slug`, and to `searchParams`, directly within your page. 00294| 00295| ## Async parameters for icon, and open-graph Image (Breaking change) 00296| 00297| > The props passed to the image generating functions in `opengraph-image`, `twitter-image`, `icon`, and `apple-icon`, are now Promises. 00298| 00299| In previous versions, both the `Image` (image generation function), and the `generateImageMetadata` received a `params` object. The `id` returned by `generateImageMetadata` was passed as a string to the image generation function. 00300| 00301| ```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js" 00302| // Next.js 15 - synchronous params access 00303| export function generateImageMetadata({ params }) { 00304| const { slug } = params 00305| return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }] 00306| } 00307| 00308| // Next.js 15 - synchronous params and id access 00309| export default function Image({ params, id }) { 00310| const slug = params.slug 00311| const imageId = id // string 00312| // ... 00313| } 00314| ``` 00315| 00316| Starting with **Next.js 16**, to align with the [Async Request APIs](#async-request-apis-breaking-change) change, the image generating function now receives `params` and `id` as promises. The `generateImageMetadata` function continues to receive synchronous `params`. 00317| 00318| ```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js" 00319| export async function generateImageMetadata({ params }) { 00320| const { slug } = params 00321| return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }] 00322| } 00323| 00324| // Next.js 16 - asynchronous params and id access 00325| export default async function Image({ params, id }) { 00326| const { slug } = await params // params now async 00327| const imageId = await id // id is now Promise when using generateImageMetadata 00328| // ... 00329| } 00330| ``` 00331| 00332| ## Async `id` parameter for `sitemap` (Breaking change) 00333| 00334| Previously, the `id` values returned from [`generateSitemaps`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-sitemaps) were passed directly to the `sitemap` generating function. 00335| 00336| ```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js" 00337| export async function generateSitemaps() { 00338| return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }] 00339| } 00340| 00341| // Next.js 15 - synchronous id access 00342| export default async function sitemap({ id }) { 00343| const start = id * 50000 // id is a number 00344| // ... 00345| } 00346| ``` 00347| 00348| Starting with **Next.js 16**, the `sitemap` generating function now receives `id` as a promise. 00349| 00350| ```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js" 00351| export async function generateSitemaps() { 00352| return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }] 00353| } 00354| 00355| // Next.js 16 - asynchronous id access 00356| export default async function sitemap({ id }) { 00357| const resolvedId = await id // id is now Promise 00358| const start = Number(resolvedId) * 50000 00359| // ... 00360| } 00361| ``` 00362| 00363| ## React 19.2 00364| 00365| The App Router in **Next.js 16** uses the latest React [Canary release](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries), which includes the newly released React 19.2 features and other features being incrementally stabilized. Highlights include: 00366| 00367| - **[View Transitions](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition)**: Animate elements that update inside a Transition or navigation 00368| - **[`useEffectEvent`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffectEvent)**: Extract non-reactive logic from Effects into reusable Effect Event functions 00369| - **[Activity](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity)**: Render "background activity" by hiding UI with `display: none` while maintaining state and cleaning up Effects 00370| 00371| Learn more in the [React 19.2 announcement](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/01/react-19-2). 00372| 00373| 00374| 00375| ## React Compiler Support 00376| 00377| Built-in support for the React Compiler is now stable in **Next.js 16** following the React Compiler's 1.0 release. The React Compiler automatically memoizes components, reducing unnecessary re-renders with zero manual code changes. 00378| 00379| The `reactCompiler` configuration option has been promoted from `experimental` to stable. It is not enabled by default as we continue gathering build performance data across different application types. 00380| 00381| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 00382| import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 00383| 00384| const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 00385| reactCompiler: true, 00386| } 00387| 00388| export default nextConfig 00389| ``` 00390| 00391| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 00392| /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 00393| const nextConfig = { 00394| reactCompiler: true, 00395| } 00396| 00397| module.exports = nextConfig 00398| ``` 00399| 00400| Install the latest version of the React Compiler plugin: 00401| 00402| ```bash package="pnpm" 00403| pnpm add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 00404| ``` 00405| 00406| ```bash package="npm" 00407| npm install -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 00408| ``` 00409| 00410| ```bash package="yarn" 00411| yarn add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 00412| ``` 00413| 00414| ```bash package="bun" 00415| bun add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 00416| ``` 00417| 00418| > **Good to know:** Expect compile times in development and during builds to be higher when enabling this option as the React Compiler relies on Babel. 00419| 00420| 00421| 00422| ## Caching APIs 00423| 00424| ### revalidateTag 00425| 00426| [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) now requires a second argument specifying a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#reference) profile. The single-argument form is deprecated and will produce a TypeScript error. 00427| 00428| ```ts 00429| // Before 00430| revalidateTag('posts') 00431| 00432| // After 00433| revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 00434| ``` 00435| 00436| If you need immediate expiration rather than stale-while-revalidate, use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) in Server Actions instead. 00437| 00438| ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 00439| 'use server' 00440| 00441| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 00442| 00443| export async function updateArticle(articleId: string) { 00444| // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 00445| revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 00446| } 00447| ``` 00448| 00449| ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 00450| 'use server' 00451| 00452| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 00453| 00454| export async function updateArticle(articleId) { 00455| // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 00456| revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 00457| } 00458| ``` 00459| 00460| Use `revalidateTag` for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, such as blog posts, product catalogs, or documentation. Users receive stale content while fresh data loads in the background. 00461| 00462| ### updateTag 00463| 00464| [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) is a new [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data#what-are-server-functions)-only API that provides **read-your-writes** semantics, where a user makes a change and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data. 00465| 00466| It does this by expiring and immediately refreshing data within the same request. 00467| 00468| ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 00469| 'use server' 00470| 00471| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 00472| 00473| export async function updateUserProfile(userId: string, profile: Profile) { 00474| await db.users.update(userId, profile) 00475| 00476| // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 00477| updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 00478| } 00479| ``` 00480| 00481| ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 00482| 'use server' 00483| 00484| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 00485| 00486| export async function updateUserProfile(userId, profile) { 00487| await db.users.update(userId, profile) 00488| 00489| // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 00490| updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 00491| } 00492| ``` 00493| 00494| This ensures interactive features reflect changes immediately. Perfect for forms, user settings, and any workflow where users expect to see their updates instantly. 00495| 00496| Learn more about when to use `updateTag` or `revalidateTag` [here](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag#when-to-use-updatetag). 00497| 00498| ### refresh 00499| 00500| [`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh) allows you to refresh the client router from within a Server Action. 00501| 00502| ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 00503| 'use server' 00504| 00505| import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 00506| 00507| export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId: string) { 00508| // Update the notification in the database 00509| await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId) 00510| 00511| // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header 00512| refresh() 00513| } 00514| ``` 00515| 00516| ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 00517| 'use server' 00518| 00519| import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 00520| 00521| export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId) { 00522| // Update the notification in the database 00523| await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId) 00524| 00525| // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header 00526| refresh() 00527| } 00528| ``` 00529| 00530| Use it when you need to refresh the client router after performing an action. 00531| 00532| ### cacheLife and cacheTag 00533| 00534| [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) are now stable. The `unstable_` prefix is no longer needed. 00535| 00536| Wherever you had aliased imports like: 00537| 00538| ```ts 00539| import { 00540| unstable_cacheLife as cacheLife, 00541| unstable_cacheTag as cacheTag, 00542| } from 'next/cache' 00543| ``` 00544| 00545| You can update your imports to: 00546| 00547| ```ts 00548| import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 00549| ``` 00550| 00551| ## Enhanced Routing and Navigation 00552| 00553| **Next.js 16** includes a complete overhaul of the routing and navigation system, making page transitions leaner and faster. This optimizes how Next.js prefetches and caches navigation data: 00554| 00555| - **Layout deduplication**: When prefetching multiple URLs with a shared layout, the layout is downloaded once. 00556| - **Incremental prefetching**: Next.js only prefetches parts not already in cache, rather than entire pages. 00557| 00558| These changes require **no code modifications** and are designed to improve performance across all apps. 00559| 00560| However, you may see more individual prefetch requests with much lower total transfer sizes. We believe this is the right trade-off for nearly all applications. 00561| 00562| If the increased request count causes issues, please let us know by creating an [issue](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues) or [discussion](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions) item. 00563| 00564| ## Partial Prerendering (PPR) 00565| 00566| **Next.js 16** removes the experimental **Partial Prerendering (PPR)** flag and configuration options, including the route level segment `experimental_ppr`. 00567| 00568| Starting with **Next.js 16**, you can opt into PPR using the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) configuration. 00569| 00570| ```js filename="next.config.js" 00571| /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 00572| const nextConfig = { 00573| cacheComponents: true, 00574| } 00575| 00576| module.exports = nextConfig 00577| ``` 00578| 00579| PPR in **Next.js 16** works differently than in **Next.js 15** canaries. If you are using PPR today, stay in the current Next.js 15 canary you are using. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) for migration patterns. 00580| 00581| ```js filename="next.config.js" 00582| /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 00583| const nextConfig = { 00584| // If you are using PPR today 00585| // stay in the current Next.js 15 canary 00586| experimental: { 00587| ppr: true, 00588| }, 00589| } 00590| 00591| module.exports = nextConfig 00592| ``` 00593| 00594| 00595| 00596| ## `middleware` to `proxy` 00597| 00598| The `middleware` filename is deprecated, and has been renamed to `proxy` to clarify network boundary and routing focus. 00599| 00600| The `edge` runtime is **NOT** supported in `proxy`. The `proxy` runtime is `nodejs`, and it cannot be configured. If you want to continue using the `edge` runtime, keep using `middleware`. description: Upgrade your Next.js Application from Version 15 to 16.

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

## Use a coding agent (recommended)

Run the latest upgrade CLI from your app's directory:

```bash filename="Terminal"
npx next@canary upgrade --agent=latest
```

The CLI prepares the Next.js 16 migration guides and codemod command for the agent, then asks it to apply the changes and verify the app. See [Upgrade with a coding agent](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/agent-upgrade) for details.

Errors can be divided into two categories: [expected errors](#handling-expected-errors) and [uncaught exceptions](#handling-uncaught-exceptions). This page will walk you through how you can handle these errors in your Next.js application.

## Handling expected errors

Expected errors are those that can occur during the normal operation of the application, such as those from [server-side form validation](/docs/app/guides/forms) or failed requests. These errors should be handled explicitly and returned to the client.

Next.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases:

- **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment.
- **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page.

## `not-found.js`

The **not-found** file renders UI when the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function is thrown within a route segment.

Before streaming starts, Next.js returns a `404` status code. After streaming starts, the status code remains `200` and the not-found UI renders in the response. Next.js injects a `<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` tag in both cases. See [Status codes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#status-codes) for details.

00002| title: generateStaticParams
00003| description: API reference for the generateStaticParams function.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
00007| 
00008| `generateStaticParams` can be used with:
00009| 
00010| - [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
00011| - [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
00012| - [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
00013| 
00014| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00015| // Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
00016| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00017|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00018| 
00019|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00020|     slug: post.slug,
00021|   }))
00022| }
00023| 
00024| // Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
00025| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00026| export default async function Page({
00027|   params,
00028| }: {
00029|   params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
00030| }) {
00031|   const { slug } = await params
00032|   // ...
00033| }
00034| ```
00035| 
00036| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00037| // Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
00038| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00039|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00040| 
00041|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00042|     slug: post.slug,
00043|   }))
00044| }
00045| 
00046| // Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
00047| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00048| export default async function Page({ params }) {
00049|   const { slug } = await params
00050|   // ...
00051| }
00052| ```
00053| 
00054| > **Good to know**:
00055| >
00056| > - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
00057| > - A dynamic route that uses [`ensureStatic = 'navigation'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic#navigation) must return at least one params object, and every object must include all dynamic parameters for the route. See the [`generateStaticParams` error guide](/docs/messages/generate-static-params#with-ensurestatic).
00058| > - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
00059| > - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
00060| > - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
00061| > - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
00062| > - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
00063| 
00064| ## Parameters
00065| 
00066| `options.params` (optional)
00067| 
00068| If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
00069| 
00070| The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
00071| 
00072| ## Returns
00073| 
00074| `generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
00075| 
00076| - Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
00077| - The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.
00078| 
00079| | Example Route                    | `generateStaticParams` Return Type        |
00080| | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
00081| | `/product/[id]`                  | `{ id: string }[]`                        |
00082| | `/products/[category]/[product]` | `{ category: string, product: string }[]` |
00083| | `/products/[...slug]`            | `{ slug: string[] }[]`                    |
00084| 
00085| ## Single Dynamic Segment
00086| 
00087| ```tsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
00088| export function generateStaticParams() {
00089|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00090| }
00091| 
00092| // Three versions of this page will be statically generated
00093| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00094| // - /product/1
00095| // - /product/2
00096| // - /product/3
00097| export default async function Page({
00098|   params,
00099| }: {
00100|   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
00101| }) {
00102|   const { id } = await params
00103|   // ...
00104| }
00105| ```
00106| 
00107| ```jsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.js" switcher

00122| 
00123| ## Multiple Dynamic Segments
00124| 
00125| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00126| export function generateStaticParams() {
00127|   return [
00128|     { category: 'a', product: '1' },
00129|     { category: 'b', product: '2' },
00130|     { category: 'c', product: '3' },
00131|   ]

00151|   return [
00152|     { category: 'a', product: '1' },
00153|     { category: 'b', product: '2' },
00154|     { category: 'c', product: '3' },
00155|   ]
00156| }
00157| 
00158| // Three versions of this page will be statically generated

00182|   params,
00183| }: {

00208| 
00209| ### Prerendering
00210| 
00211| #### All paths at build time
00212| 
00213| To statically render all paths at build time, supply the full list of paths to `generateStaticParams`:

00280| 
00281| export async function generateStaticParams() {

00284|

00292| 
00293| To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):

00297|   return []
00298| }

00302| >
00303| > - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
00304| 
00305| ```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"

00308| 
00309| #### With Cache Components
00310| 
00311| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
00312| 
00313| > **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
00314| 
00315| See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs, or [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for prerendering a subset of routes and serving App Shells for the rest.
00316| 
00317| ### With Route Handlers
00318| 
00319| You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
00320| 
00321| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher
00322| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00323|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00324| }
00325| 
00326| export async function GET(
00327|   request: Request,
00328|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00329| ) {
00330|   const { id } = await params
00331|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00332|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00333| }
00334| ```
00335| 
00336| ```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher
00337| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00338|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00339| }
00340| 
00341| export async function GET(request, { params }) {
00342|   const { id } = await params
00343|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00344|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00345| }
00346| ```
00347| 
00348| ### Route Handlers with Cache Components
00349| 
00350| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:
00351| 
00352| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"
00353| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00354|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00355| }
00356| 
00357| async function getPost(id: Promise<string>) {
00358|   'use cache'
00359|   const resolvedId = await id
00360|   const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/posts/${resolvedId}`)
00361|   return response.json()
00362| }
00363| 
00364| export async function GET(
00365|   request: Request,
00366|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00367| ) {
00368|   const post = await getPost(params.then((p) => p.id))
00369|   return Response.json(post)
00370| }
00371| ```
00372| 
00373| See the [Route Handlers documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#static-generation-with-generatestaticparams) for more details.
00374| 
00375| ### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
00376| 
00377| To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).
00378| 
00379| ### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
00380| 
00381| You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
00382| 
00383| - `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
00384| - `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.
00385| 
00386| There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
00387| 
00388| #### Generate params from the bottom up
00389| 
00390| Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.
00391| 
00392| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00393| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00394| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00395|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00396| 
00397|   return products.map((product) => ({
00398|     category: product.category.slug,
00399|     product: product.id,
00400|   }))
00401| }
00402| 
00403| export default function Page({
00404|   params,
00405| }: {
00406|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00407| }) {
00408|   // ...
00409| }
00410| ```
00411| 
00412| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00413| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00414| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00415|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00416| 
00417|   return products.map((product) => ({
00418|     category: product.category.slug,
00419|     product: product.id,
00420|   }))
00421| }
00422| 
00423| export default function Page({ params }) {
00424|   // ...
00425| }
00426| ```
00427| 
00428| #### Generate params from the top down
00429| 
00430| Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
00431| 
00432| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher
00433| // Generate segments for [category]
00434| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00435|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00436| 
00437|   return products.map((product) => ({
00438|     category: product.category.slug,
00439|   }))
00440| }
00441| 
00442| export default function Layout({
00443|   params,
00444| }: {
00445|   params: Promise<{ category: string }>
00446| }) {
00447|   // ...
00448| }
00449| ```
00450| 
00451| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
00452| // Generate segments for [category]
00453| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00454|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00455| 
00456|   return products.map((product) => ({
00457|     category: product.category.slug,
00458|   }))
00459| }
00460| 
00461| export default function Layout({ params }) {
00462|   // ...
00463| }
00464| ```
00465| 
00466| A child route segment's `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each segment a parent `generateStaticParams` generates.
00467| 
00468| The child `generateStaticParams` function can use the `params` returned from the parent `generateStaticParams` function to dynamically generate its own segments.
00469| 
00470| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00471| // Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
00472| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
00473| export async function generateStaticParams({
00474|   params: { category },
00475| }: {
00476|   params: { category: string }
00477| }) {
00478|   const products = await fetch(
00479|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00480|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00481| 
00482|   return products.map((product) => ({
00483|     product: product.id,
00484|   }))
00485| }
00486| 
00487| export default function Page({
00488|   params,
00489| }: {
00490|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00491| }) {
00492|   // ...
00493| }
00494| ```
00495| 
00496| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00497| // Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
00498| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
00499| export async function generateStaticParams({ params: { category } }) {
00500|   const products = await fetch(
00501|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00502|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00503| 
00504|   return products.map((product) => ({
00505|     product: product.id,
00506|   }))
00507| }
00508| 
00509| export default function Page({ params }) {
00510|   // ...
00511| }
00512| ```
00513| 
00514| Notice that the params argument can be accessed synchronously and includes only parent segment params.
00515| 
00516| > **Good to know:** When a parent dynamic segment is a [root parameter](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), you can also read it inside a nested `generateStaticParams` by calling its getter from the `next/root-params` module.
00517| 
00518| For type completion, you can make use of the TypeScript `Awaited` helper in combination with either [`Page Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`Layout Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper):
00519| 
00520| ```ts filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00521| export async function generateStaticParams({
00522|   params: { category },
00523| }: {
00524|   params: Awaited<LayoutProps<'/products/[category]'>['params']>
00525| }) {
00526|   const products = await fetch(
00527|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00528|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00529| 
00530|   return products.map((product) => ({
00531|     product: product.id,
00532|   }))
00533| }
00534| ```
00535| 
00536| > **Good to know**: `fetch` requests are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across all `generate`-prefixed functions, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
00537| 
00538| ## Version History
00539| 
00540| | Version   | Changes                            |
00541| | --------- | ---------------------------------- |
00542| | `v13.0.0` | `generateStaticParams` introduced. |
00543|

00042| ## `generateMetadata` function
00043| 
00044| Dynamic metadata depends on **dynamic information**, such as the current route parameters, external data, or `metadata` in parent segments, can be set by exporting a `generateMetadata` function that returns a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields).
00045| 
00046| Resolving `generateMetadata` is part of rendering the page. If the page can be prerendered and `generateMetadata` doesn't introduce dynamic behavior, the resulting metadata is included in the page's initial HTML.
00047| 
00048| Otherwise the metadata resolved from `generateMetadata` [can be streamed](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#streaming-metadata) after sending the initial UI.

00050| ```tsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.tsx" switcher

00052| 
00053| type Props = {
00054|   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
00055|   searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
00056| }
00057| 
00058| export async function generateMetadata(
00059|   { params, searchParams }: Props,
00060|   parent: ResolvingMetadata
00061| ): Promise<Metadata> {

00063|   const { id } = await params
00064| 
00065|   // fetch data
00066|   const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
00067| 
00068|   // optionally access and extend (rather than replace) parent metadata
00069|   const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []
00070| 
00071|   return {
00072|     title: product.title,
00073|     openGraph: {
00074|       images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],

00086|

00163| ## Reference

00165| ### Parameters
00166| 
00167| `generateMetadata` function accepts the following parameters:
00168| 
00169| - `props` - An object containing the parameters of the current route:
00170|   - `params` - An object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to the segment `generateMetadata` is called from. Examples:
00171|

00173|     | ------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------- |
00174|     | `app/shop/[slug]/page.js`       | `/shop/1`   | `{ slug: '1' }`           |
00175|     | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/page.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `{ tag: '1', item: '2' }` |
00176|     | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js`    | `/shop/1/2` | `{ slug: ['1', '2'] }`    |

00182|     | `/shop?a=1`     | `{ a: '1' }`         |
00183|     | `/shop?a=1&b=2` | `{ a: '1', b: '2' }` |
00184|     | `/shop?a=1&a=2` | `{ a: ['1', '2'] }`  |

00195| > - `fetch` requests are automatically memoized for the same data across `generateMetadata`, `generateStaticParams`, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
00196| > - `searchParams` are only available in `page.js` segments.
00197| > - The [`redirect()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect) and [`notFound()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) Next.js methods can also be used inside `generateMetadata`.
00198| 
00199| ### Metadata Fields
00200| 
00201| The following fields are supported:
00202| 
00203| #### `title`
00204| 
00205| The `title` attribute is used to set the title of the document. It can be defined as a simple [string](#string) or an optional [template object](#template).
00206| 
00207| ##### String
00208| 
00209| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
00210| export const metadata = {
00211|   title: 'Next.js',
00212| }
00213| ```
00214| 
00215| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
00216| <title>Next.js</title>
00217| ```
00218| 
00219| ##### `default`
00220| 
00221| `title.default` can be used to provide a **fallback title** to child route segments that don't define a `title`.
00222| 
00223| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx"
00224| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00225| 
00226| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00227|   title: {
00228|     default: 'Acme',
00229|   },
00230| }
00231| ```
00232| 
00233| ```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx"
00234| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00235| 
00236| export const metadata: Metadata = {}
00237| 
00238| // Output: <title>Acme</title>
00239| ```
00240| 
00241| ##### `template`
00242| 
00243| `title.template` can be used to add a prefix or a suffix to `titles` defined in **child** route segments.
00244| 
00245| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00246| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00247| 
00248| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00249|   title: {
00250|     template: '%s | Acme',
00251|     default: 'Acme', // a default is required when creating a template
00252|   },
00253| }
00254| ```
00255| 
00256| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00257| export const metadata = {
00258|   title: {
00259|     template: '%s | Acme',
00260|     default: 'Acme', // a default is required when creating a template
00261|   },
00262| }
00263| ```
00264| 
00265| ```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx" switcher
00266| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00267| 
00268| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00269|   title: 'About',
00270| }
00271| 
00272| // Output: <title>About | Acme</title>
00273| ```
00274| 
00275| ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js" switcher
00276| export const metadata = {
00277|   title: 'About',
00278| }
00279| 
00280| // Output: <title>About | Acme</title>
00281| ```
00282| 
00283| > **Good to know**:
00284| >
00285| > - `title.template` applies to **child** route segments and **not** the segment it's defined in. This means:
00286| >   - `title.default` is **required** when you add a `title.template`.
00287| >   - `title.template` defined in `layout.js` will not apply to a `title` defined in a `page.js` of the same route segment.
00288| >   - `title.template` defined in `page.js` has no effect because a page is always the terminating segment (it doesn't have any children route segments).
00289| > - `title.template` has **no effect** if a route has not defined a `title` or `title.default`.
00290| 
00291| ##### `absolute`
00292| 
00293| `title.absolute` can be used to provide a title that **ignores** `title.template` set in parent segments.
00294| 
00295| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00296| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00297| 
00298| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00299|   title: {
00300|     template: '%s | Acme',
00301|   },
00302| }
00303| ```
00304| 
00305| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00306| export const metadata = {
00307|   title: {
00308|     template: '%s | Acme',
00309|   },
00310| }
00311| ```
00312| 
00313| ```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx" switcher
00314| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00315| 
00316| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00317|   title: {
00318|     absolute: 'About',
00319|   },
00320| }
00321| 
00322| // Output: <title>About</title>
00323| ```
00324| 
00325| ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js" switcher
00326| export const metadata = {
00327|   title: {
00328|     absolute: 'About',
00329|   },
00330| }
00331| 
00332| // Output: <title>About</title>
00333| ```
00334| 
00335| > **Good to know**:
00336| >
00337| > - `layout.js`
00338| >   - `title` (string) and `title.default` define the default title for child segments (that do not define their own `title`). It will augment `title.template` from the closest parent segment if it exists.
00339| >   - `title.absolute` defines the default title for child segments. It ignores `title.template` from parent segments.
00340| >   - `title.template` defines a new title template for child segments.
00341| > - `page.js`
00342| >   - If a page does not define its own title the closest parents resolved title will be used.
00343| >   - `title` (string) defines the routes title. It will augment `title.template` from the closest parent segment if it exists.
00344| >   - `title.absolute` defines the route title. It ignores `title.template` from parent segments.
00345| >   - `title.template` has no effect in `page.js` because a page is always the terminating segment of a route.
00346|

00391| #### `metadataBase`
00392| 
00393| `metadataBase` is a convenience option to set a base URL prefix for `metadata` fields that require a fully qualified URL.
00394| 
00395| - `metadataBase` allows URL-based `metadata` fields defined in the **current route segment and below** to use a **relative path** instead of an otherwise required absolute URL.
00396| - The field's relative path will be composed with `metadataBase` to form a fully qualified URL.
00397| 
00398| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
00399| export const metadata = {
00400|   metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
00401|   alternates: {
00402|     canonical: '/',
00403|     languages: {
00404|       'en-US': '/en-US',
00405|       'de-DE': '/de-DE',
00406|     },
00407|   },
00408|   openGraph: {
00409|     images: '/og-image.png',
00410|   },
00411| }
00412| ```
00413| 
00414| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
00415| <link rel="canonical" href="https://acme.com" />
00416| <link rel="alternate" hreflang="en-US" href="https://acme.com/en-US" />
00417| <link rel="alternate" hreflang="de-DE" href="https://acme.com/de-DE" />
00418| <meta property="og:image" content="https://acme.com/og-image.png" />
00419| ```
00420| 
00421| > **Good to know**:
00422| >
00423| > - `metadataBase` is typically set in root `app/layout.js` to apply to URL-based `metadata` fields across all routes.
00424| > - When `generateMetadata` uses `'use cache'`, its return value must be serializable. `URL` instances are not supported by Cache Functions, so values such as `metadataBase` should be returned as strings (for example, `url.toString()`). See [`use cache` serialization requirements](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#serialization).
00425| > - All URL-based `metadata` fields that require absolute URLs can be configured with a `metadataBase` option.
00426| > - `metadataBase` can contain a subdomain e.g. `https://app.acme.com` or base path e.g. `https://acme.com/start/from/here`
00427| > - If a `metadata` field provides an absolute URL, `metadataBase` will be ignored.
00428| > - Using a relative path in a URL-based `metadata` field without configuring a `metadataBase` will cause a build error.
00429| > - Next.js will normalize duplicate slashes between `metadataBase` (e.g. `https://acme.com/`) and a relative field (e.g. `/path`) to a single slash (e.g. `https://acme.com/path`)
00430| 
00431| #### URL Composition
00432| 
00433| URL composition favors developer intent over default directory traversal semantics.
00434| 
00435| - Trailing slashes between `metadataBase` and `metadata` fields are normalized.
00436| - An "absolute" path in a `metadata` field (that typically would replace the whole URL path) is treated as a "relative" path (starting from the end of `metadataBase`).
00437| 
00438| For example, given the following `metadataBase`:
00439| 
00440| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00441| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00442| 
00443| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00444|   metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
00445| }
00446| ```
00447| 
00448| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00449| export const metadata = {
00450|   metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
00451| }
00452| ```
00453| 
00454| Any `metadata` fields that inherit the above `metadataBase` and set their own value will be resolved as follows:
00455| 
00456| | `metadata` field                 | Resolved URL                     |
00457| | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
00458| | `/`                              | `https://acme.com`               |
00459| | `./`                             | `https://acme.com`               |
00460| | `payments`                       | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
00461| | `/payments`                      | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
00462| | `./payments`                     | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
00463| | `../payments`                    | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
00464| | `https://beta.acme.com/payments` | `https://beta.acme.com/payments` |
00465|

01048| ### Types
01049| 
01050| You can add type safety to your metadata by using the `Metadata` type. If you are using the [built-in TypeScript plugin](/docs/app/api-reference/config/typescript) in your IDE, you do not need to manually add the type, but you can still explicitly add it if you want.
01051| 
01052| #### `metadata` object
01053| 
01054| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
01055| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
01056| 
01057| export const metadata: Metadata = {
01058|   title: 'Next.js',
01059| }
01060| ```
01061| 
01062| #### `generateMetadata` function
01063| 
01064| ##### Regular function
01065| 
01066| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
01067| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
01068| 
01069| export function generateMetadata(): Metadata {
01070|   return {
01071|     title: 'Next.js',
01072|   }
01073| }
01074| ```
01075| 
01076| ##### Async function
01077| 
01078| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
01079| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
01080| 
01081| export async function generateMetadata(): Promise<Metadata> {
01082|   return {
01083|     title: 'Next.js',
01084|   }
01085| }

01087| 
01088| ##### With segment props
01089| 
01090| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
01091| import type { Metadata } from 'next'

01094|   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
01095|   searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
01096| }
01097|

01099|   return {
01100|     title: 'Next.js',
01101|   }
01102| }
01103| 
01104| export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
01105| ```
01106|

01108|

01110| import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
01111| 
01112| export async function generateMetadata(
01113|   { params, searchParams }: Props,
01114|   parent: ResolvingMetadata
01115| ): Promise<Metadata> {
01116|   return {
01117|     title: 'Next.js',
01118|   }
01119| }

01123|

01125| 
01126| ```js filename="layout.js | page.js"
01127| /** @type {import("next").Metadata} */

01129|   title: 'Next.js',

01132| 
01133| ### Unsupported Metadata
01134| 
01135| The following metadata types do not currently have built-in support. However, they can still be rendered in the layout or page itself.
01136| 
01137| | Metadata                      | Recommendation                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
01138| | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
01139| | `<meta http-equiv="...">`     | Use appropriate HTTP Headers via [`redirect()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect), [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy#nextresponse), [Security Headers](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/headers) |
01140| | `<base>`                      | Render the tag in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
01141| | `<noscript>`                  | Render the tag in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
01142| | `<style>`                     | Learn more about [styling in Next.js](/docs/app/getting-started/css).                                                                                                                                                                        |
01143| | `<script>`                    | Learn more about [using scripts](/docs/app/guides/scripts).                                                                                                                                                                                  |
01144| | `<link rel="stylesheet" />`   | `import` stylesheets directly in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
01145| | `<link rel="preload" />`      | Use [ReactDOM preload method](#link-relpreload)                                                                                                                                                                                              |
01146| | `<link rel="preconnect" />`   | Use [ReactDOM preconnect method](#link-relpreconnect)                                                                                                                                                                                        |
01147| | `<link rel="dns-prefetch" />` | Use [ReactDOM prefetchDNS method](#link-reldns-prefetch)                                                                                                                                                                                     |
01148| 
01149| ### Resource hints
01150| 
01151| The `<link>` element has a number of `rel` keywords that can be used to hint to the browser that an external resource is likely to be needed. The browser uses this information to apply preloading optimizations depending on the keyword.
01152| 
01153| While the Metadata API doesn't directly support these hints, you can use new [`ReactDOM` methods](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/26237) to safely insert them into the `<head>` of the document.
01154| 
01155| ```tsx filename="app/preload-resources.tsx" switcher
01156| 'use client'
01157| 
01158| import ReactDOM from 'react-dom'
01159| 
01160| export function PreloadResources() {
01161|   ReactDOM.preload('...', { as: '...' })
01162|   ReactDOM.preconnect('...', { crossOrigin: '...' })
01163|   ReactDOM.prefetchDNS('...')
01164| 
01165|   return '...'
01166| }
01167| ```
01168| 
01169| ```jsx filename="app/preload-resources.js" switcher
01170| 'use client'
01171| 
01172| import ReactDOM from 'react-dom'
01173| 
01174| export function PreloadResources() {
01175|   ReactDOM.preload('...', { as: '...' })
01176|   ReactDOM.preconnect('...', { crossOrigin: '...' })
01177|   ReactDOM.prefetchDNS('...')
01178| 
01179|   return '...'
01180| }
01181| ```
01182| 
01183| #### `<link rel="preload">`
01184| 
01185| Start loading a resource early in the page rendering (browser) lifecycle. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/preload).
01186| 
01187| ```tsx
01188| ReactDOM.preload(href: string, options: { as: string })
01189| ```
01190| 
01191| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
01192| <link rel="preload" href="..." as="..." />
01193| ```
01194| 
01195| ##### `<link rel="preconnect">`
01196| 
01197| Preemptively initiate a connection to an origin. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/preconnect).
01198| 
01199| ```tsx
01200| ReactDOM.preconnect(href: string, options?: { crossOrigin?: string })
01201| ```
01202| 
01203| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
01204| <link rel="preconnect" href="..." crossorigin />
01205| ```
01206| 
01207| #### `<link rel="dns-prefetch">`
01208| 
01209| Attempt to resolve a domain name before resources get requested. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/dns-prefetch).
01210| 
01211| ```tsx
01212| ReactDOM.prefetchDNS(href: string)
01213| ```
01214| 
01215| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
01216| <link rel="dns-prefetch" href="..." />
01217| ```
01218| 
01219| > **Good to know**:
01220| >
01221| > - These methods are currently only supported in Client Components, which are still Server Side Rendered on initial page load.
01222| > - Next.js in-built features such as `next/font`, `next/image` and `next/script` automatically handle relevant resource hints.
01223| 
01224| ## Behavior
01225| 
01226| ### Default Fields
01227| 
01228| There are two default `meta` tags that are always added even if a route doesn't define metadata:
01229| 
01230| - The [meta charset tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset) sets the character encoding for the website.
01231| - The [meta viewport tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag) sets the viewport width and scale for the website to adjust for different devices.
01232| 
01233| ```html
01234| <meta charset="utf-8" />
01235| <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
01236| ```
01237| 
01238| > **Good to know**: You can overwrite the default [`viewport`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#viewport) meta tag.
01239| 
01240| ### Streaming metadata
01241| 
01242| Streaming metadata allows Next.js to render and send the initial UI to the browser, without waiting for `generateMetadata` to complete.
01243| 
01244| When `generateMetadata` resolves, the resulting metadata tags are appended to the `<body>` tag. We have verified that metadata is interpreted correctly by bots that execute JavaScript and inspect the full DOM (e.g. `Googlebot`).
01245| 
01246| For **HTML-limited bots** that can’t execute JavaScript (e.g. `facebookexternalhit`), metadata continues to block page rendering. The resulting metadata will be available in the `<head>` tag.
01247| 
01248| Next.js automatically detects **HTML-limited bots** by looking at the User Agent header. You can use the [`htmlLimitedBots`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/htmlLimitedBots) option in your Next.js config file to override the default [User Agent list](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/shared/lib/router/utils/html-bots.ts).
01249| 
01250| To fully disable streaming metadata:
01251| 
01252| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
01253| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
01254| 
01255| const config: NextConfig = {
01256|   htmlLimitedBots: /.*/,
01257| }
01258| 
01259| export default config
01260| ```
01261| 
01262| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
01263| module.exports = {
01264|   htmlLimitedBots: /.*/,
01265| }
01266| ```
01267| 
01268| Streaming metadata improves perceived performance by reducing [TTFB](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Time_to_first_byte) and can help lowering [LCP](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Largest_contentful_paint) time.
01269| 
01270| Overriding `htmlLimitedBots` could lead to longer response times. Streaming metadata is an advanced feature, and the default should be sufficient for most cases.
01271| 
01272| ### With Cache Components
01273| 
01274| When [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) is enabled, `generateMetadata` follows the same rules as other components. If metadata accesses runtime data (`cookies()`, `headers()`, `params`, `searchParams`) or performs uncached data fetching, it defers to request time.
01275| 
01276| How Next.js handles this depends on the rest of your page:
01277| 
01278| - **If other parts also defer to request time**: Prerendering generates a static shell, and metadata streams in with other deferred content.
01279| - **If the page or layout is otherwise fully prerenderable**: Next.js requires an explicit choice: cache the data if possible, or signal that deferred rendering is intentional.
01280| 
01281| Streaming metadata at runtime while the rest of the page is fully prerenderable is not common. To ensure this behavior is intentional, an error is raised indicating which page or layout needs to be handled.
01282| 
01283| To resolve this, you have two options. If metadata depends on external data but not runtime data, use `use cache`:
01284| 
01285| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={2}
01286| export async function generateMetadata() {
01287|   'use cache'
01288|   const { title, description } = await db.query('site-metadata')
01289|   return { title, description }
01290| }
01291| ```
01292| 
01293| If metadata genuinely requires runtime data, add a dynamic marker component to your page:
01294| 
01295| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={11-14,19,31}
01296| import { Suspense } from 'react'
01297| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
01298| import { connection } from 'next/server'
01299| 
01300| export async function generateMetadata() {
01301|   const token = (await cookies()).get('token')?.value
01302|   // ... use token to fetch personalized metadata
01303|   return { title: 'Personalized Title' }
01304| }
01305| 
01306| const Connection = async () => {
01307|   await connection()
01308|   return null
01309| }
01310| 
01311| async function DynamicMarker() {
01312|   return (
01313|     <Suspense>
01314|       <Connection />
01315|     </Suspense>
01316|   )
01317| }
01318| 
01319| export default function Page() {
01320|   // DO NOT place await connection() here
01321|   // doing so prevents the article tag content from
01322|   // being included in the static shell
01323|   return (
01324|     <>
01325|       <article>Static content</article>
01326|       <DynamicMarker />
01327|     </>
01328|   )
01329| }
01330| ```
01331| 
01332| The `DynamicMarker` component renders nothing but tells Next.js the page has intentional dynamic content. By wrapping it in Suspense, the static content still prerenders normally.
01333| 
01334| See [Next.js encountered runtime data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-runtime) and [Next.js encountered uncached data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-dynamic) for full fix options and trade-offs.
01335| 
01336| ### Ordering
01337| 
01338| Metadata is evaluated in order, starting from the root segment down to the segment closest to the final `page.js` segment. For example:
01339| 
01340| 1. `app/layout.tsx` (Root Layout)
01341| 2. `app/blog/layout.tsx` (Nested Blog Layout)
01342| 3. `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` (Blog Page)
01343| 
01344| ### Merging
01345| 
01346| Following the [evaluation order](#ordering), Metadata objects exported from multiple segments in the same route are **shallowly** merged together to form the final metadata output of a route. Duplicate keys are **replaced** based on their ordering.
01347| 
01348| This means metadata with nested fields such as [`openGraph`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#opengraph) and [`robots`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#robots) that are defined in an earlier segment are **overwritten** by the last segment to define them.
01349| 
01350| #### Overwriting fields
01351| 
01352| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js"
01353| export const metadata = {
01354|   title: 'Acme',
01355|   openGraph: {
01356|     title: 'Acme',
01357|     description: 'Acme is a...',
01358|   },
01359| }
01360| ```
01361| 
01362| ```jsx filename="app/blog/page.js"
01363| export const metadata = {
01364|   title: 'Blog',
01365|   openGraph: {
01366|     title: 'Blog',
01367|   },
01368| }
01369| 
01370| // Output:
01371| // <title>Blog</title>
01372| // <meta property="og:title" content="Blog" />
01373| ```
01374| 
01375| In the example above:
01376| 
01377| - `title` from `app/layout.js` is **replaced** by `title` in `app/blog/page.js`.
01378| - All `openGraph` fields from `app/layout.js` are **replaced** in `app/blog/page.js` because `app/blog/page.js` sets `openGraph` metadata. Note the absence of `openGraph.description`.
01379| 
01380| If you'd like to share some nested fields between segments while overwriting others, you can pull them out into a separate variable:
01381| 
01382| ```jsx filename="app/shared-metadata.js"
01383| export const openGraphImage = { images: ['http://...'] }
01384| ```
01385| 
01386| ```jsx filename="app/page.js"
01387| import { openGraphImage } from './shared-metadata'
01388| 
01389| export const metadata = {
01390|   openGraph: {
01391|     ...openGraphImage,
01392|     title: 'Home',
01393|   },
01394| }
01395| ```
01396| 
01397| ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js"
01398| import { openGraphImage } from '../shared-metadata'
01399| 
01400| export const metadata = {
01401|   openGraph: {
01402|     ...openGraphImage,
01403|     title: 'About',
01404|   },
01405| }
01406| ```
01407| 
01408| In the example above, the OG image is shared between `app/layout.js` and `app/about/page.js` while the titles are different.
01409| 
01410| #### Inheriting fields
01411| 
01412| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js"
01413| export const metadata = {
01414|   title: 'Acme',
01415|   openGraph: {
01416|     title: 'Acme',
01417|     description: 'Acme is a...',
01418|   },
01419| }
01420| ```
01421| 
01422| ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js"
01423| export const metadata = {
01424|   title: 'About',
01425| }
01426| 
01427| // Output:
01428| // <title>About</title>
01429| // <meta property="og:title" content="Acme" />
01430| // <meta property="og:description" content="Acme is a..." />
01431| ```
01432| 
01433| **Notes**
01434| 
01435| - `title` from `app/layout.js` is **replaced** by `title` in `app/about/page.js`.
01436| - All `openGraph` fields from `app/layout.js` are **inherited** in `app/about/page.js` because `app/about/page.js` doesn't set `openGraph` metadata.
01437| 
01438| ## Version History
01439| 
01440| | Version   | Changes                                                                                                                                                 |
01441| | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
01442| | `v15.2.0` | Introduced streaming support to `generateMetadata`.                                                                                                     |
01443| | `v14.0.0` | `viewport`, `themeColor`, and `colorScheme` deprecated in favor of the [`viewport` configuration](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-viewport). |
01444| | `v13.2.0` | `metadata` and `generateMetadata` introduced.                                                                                                           |

To define static metadata, export a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields) from a `layout.js` or `page.js` file.

All routes and files have been migrated from the Pages Router to the Next.js App Router with TypeScript types, and the `pages` directory has been removed:

- **Layout & Providers**: Replaced `pages/_app.js` and `pages/_document.js` with `app/layout.tsx` (using `next/font/google` for `Inter` and Metadata API) and migrated `components/AppProvider.tsx` to a typed Client Component.
- **Pages**:
  - `pages/index.js` → `app/page.tsx` + `app/HomeClient.tsx` (using `await headers()` from `next/headers`, `cache: 'no-store'`, `metadata`, and `useRouter` from `next/navigation`).
  - `pages/blog/index.js` → `app/blog/page.tsx` + `app/blog/BlogListClient.tsx` (using ISR `revalidate = 60`, `metadata`, and `useRouter` from `next/navigation`).
  - `pages/blog/[id].js` → `app/blog/[id]/page.tsx` + `app/blog/[id]/BlogPostClient.tsx` (using `generateStaticParams`, `dynamicParams = true`, `revalidate = 300`, `generateMetadata`, async `params`, and `notFound()`).
- **Error & Not Found**: Replaced `pages/_error.js` and `pages/404.js` with `app/error.tsx`, `app/global-error.tsx`, and `app/not-found.tsx` (`app/NotFoundClient.tsx`).
- **API Routes**: Replaced `pages/api/posts/index.js` and `pages/api/posts/[id].js` with Web API Route Handlers in `app/api/posts/route.ts` and `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts`.
